text:
1	# Prelude
2	
3	A tool for designing (and later building) apps with an agent: pick a folder,
4	chat with an agent, watch the design appear. The plan, its ground rules and
5	every decision taken are in `docs/plan.md`. Read it before adding a feature.
6	Nothing gets added until we've decided where it fits in the simple model
7	(folder, design, session, screen; a chat surface and a design surface).
8	
9	## Koda
10	
11	This application is built with Koda. Before writing or changing a view, a
12	stylesheet or a handler, load the matching skill - `koda-app-authoring`,
13	`koda-styling`, `koda-server-setup` (and `koda-composition` for anything that
14	crosses an application or a host) - and follow it. Look attributes up in the
15	Koda reference (`node_modules/@kodalang/core/docs/reference.md`, the version
16	Prelude depends on) rather than from memory. Run `koda-review` before calling a
17	change finished.
18	
19	Koda is the npm package `@kodalang/core`, pinned in `package.json`, and it ships
20	its skills. The ones in `.claude/skills/` are copies of the installed package's;
21	`test/skills.test.js` fails when they differ. After upgrading Koda, run
22	`npm run skills` to copy them again, and read what changed.
23	
24	## Working here
25	
26	- `npm start` runs Prelude on http://localhost:4200 (`PORT` to change it).
27	  Views are cached when the server starts: restart it after changing one.
28	- `npm test` runs the tests (node --test). Add tests for what you build.
29	- The desktop app: `npm run build:shell` builds `tauri/src-tauri` (about 10
30	  minutes from cold) into `dist-shell/Prelude.exe`. `npm run test:shell` runs its
31	  Rust tests. The app is a window on the server: it uses one already answering
32	  `/health` on localhost:4200 (`npm start`), or else starts `node start.js`
33	  itself (Prelude's folder is found above the exe, or `--root`/`PRELUDE_ROOT`;
34	  its output goes to `~/.prelude/server.log`) and stops it on quit. `--server
35	  <url>` or `PRELUDE_URL` p

1	# Prelude Shell - notes
2	
3	Prelude's own app shell: the layouts Prelude's pages render in. Drafted from
4	what Prelude ships (`server/views/layout.eta`, the `.bar`/`.page`/`.workspace`
5	rules in `server/public/prelude.css`, and the pop-out `_window.eta`), on the
6	Prelude Design System. Gallery: `/gallery` (with `/drawer`, `/modal`,
7	`/notice` over it), `/gallery/workspace`, `/gallery/window`.
8	
9	## Layouts
10	
11	- **app** - the bar, then the page scrolling with the window. Pages hold their
12	  own width (`.center`); the shell gives the room above and below. Projects, a
13	  project, Build.
14	- **workspace** - the bar, then the page filling the rest of the window; the
15	  window doesn't scroll, the page's panels do. A design's page (chat + surface).
16	- **window** - no bar; the page fills the window. The pop-out design surface.
17	
18	Shared parts in `layouts/` (`_head`, `_bar`, `_agents`, `_regions`), since a layout's
19	includes resolve from there. Chrome CSS is `layouts/shell.css`, all in the
20	`host` layer, styling only `.shell-*`. `styles.css` is the gallery's alone.
21	
22	## Decisions
23	
24	- **The gallery shows placeholders, not content** (Prelude's guidance,
25	  2026-10-16): grey `.skeleton` blocks (styles.css) wherever a page or an
26	  overlay puts content, so what's real on screen is the layout's. The only
27	  real content is the buttons that open each region. Placeholder headings keep
28	  a hidden name ("Sample drawer", "Sample question"), so the dialog is still
29	  named and the Close still lines up. States hold only layout data now.
30	- **"Project", not "folder"** (the person's decision, 2026-10-16), in every
31	  word the shell shows and in its data (`it.layout.projects`, `agents[].project`).
32	  URLs keep `/f/<id>`: they're the app's routes, not words. A folder the agent
33	  may read (not the project) is still a folder. The design system's
34	  guidelines.md still says "folder, not project" in its Words table: it needs
35	  cha

I've connected the app. It's Prelude's own server in `server/`, written in Node with `node:http`, Eta and Koda. I didn't change any of the app's files, and I couldn't render anything myself, so the next message will show whether the gallery renders.

**What I changed:**
- **`prelude/prelude.json`**: kept `"existing": true` and added `"path": "server"` and `"stack": "Node, node:http, Eta and Koda"`.
- **`prelude/prelude-shell/layouts.json`**: maps the shell's `app` layout to `@app/server/views/layout`. That's the app's only layout file. It reads `it.body`, `it.path` and `it.title`, which Prelude passes to a layout.
- **No design host.** The app's views are plain Eta with nothing of its own needed to render them; data like an entry's `html` is prepared in `server/views.js` beforehand. So Prelude renders them itself.

**Layouts that stay the shell's:** `workspace` and `window`. The app has no separate file for either. Its one `layout.eta` makes the window with a `bare` flag, and the workspace comes from `:has(.session-page)` rules in `prelude.css`. `layouts.json` can only point to a file, not set a flag.

**Where the app's layout differs from the design** (in `prelude/prelude-shell/NOTES.md`, nothing changed):
- **No overlays.** It has no `notice`, `drawer` or `modal` regions, so the three overlay pages of the gallery will show only the page underneath.
- **Bar:** just the brand, with no Projects menu or agent status.
- **Main area:** its id is `#workspace`, not `#main`.
- **Styles may be missing.** The layout loads its CSS from `/ds/v1/…` (KodaDesign's copy, not this project's design system) and `/static/prelude.css`, and Koda from `/koda/koda.js`. Those addresses belong to the app, not to the design's preview, so the gallery may render without styles or Koda. The shell's `shell.css` isn't loaded at all.
Committed to prelude/prelude-shell (deb13f9).
